src/rebar/_commands/delete.py:173 `def _git(...)` calls run_git_write; callers at :326/:329/:352/:353 do `_git(tracker,"add"...)`/`_git(tracker,"commit"...)`
src/rebar/_commands/compact.py:58 `def _git` -> run_git_write; 6 mutation callers at :374/:381/:553/:559/:745/:751

findings.finding: The plan's load-bearing premise 'The raw sites at HEAD are few and verified' is materially false: many additional legitimate store-write sites route through per-module local _git wrappers (which themselves call run_git_write) and will fire under R2's by-name flagging, each needing a marker the plan does not enumerate.
findings.location: Approach — 'The raw sites at HEAD are few and verified'; Scope — 'inline markers on the enumerated seam internals'; AC line 'All enumerated seam internals ... are marked with reasons; tree is clean at landing'
scenarios: Implementer marks only the ~5 enumerated sites, then the first full-tree scan is RED with dozens of unmarked hits across delete/compact/txn/init/fsck_*
The 'tree is clean at landing' AC cannot be satisfied without discovering and marking the full set the plan did not enumerate
findings.suggested_fix: Replace the fixed 5-site enumeration with an instruction to enumerate every raw/wrapped mutation site by running the two rules across the tree first, and expand the marker-target list in Scope to include _commands/delete.py, compact.py, txn.py (STATUS/CLAIM callers), init.py bootstrap, fsck_repair.py, fsck_recover.py.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Correct the 'four wrapper names' claim to reflect that `_git` is defined in multiple modules (delete/compact/txn/init/fsck_repair/fsck_recover/fsck) and that R2's by-name flag fires on every such caller, then confirm the lint's wrapper-name set and marker targets cover them all.
evidence: search 'def _git' returns delete.py:173, compact.py:58, fsck_repair.py:56, fsck_recover.py:61, txn.py:119, fsck.py:386, init.py:80 — each a distinct local `_git`

findings.finding: The plan states there are exactly 'four wrapper names at HEAD (run_git, run_git_write, _run_git, _git)', but `_git` is defined in 7+ modules with different signatures/bodies; the by-name R2 rule will fire on all of them, and the plan's single-wrapper framing misrepresents the surface it must handle.
findings.location: Approach — R2 'the four wrapper names at HEAD, listed in the lint'
scenarios: A future author reads the plan expecting `_git` to be one known wrapper and mis-scopes the lint's name list or the marking effort

findings.finding: The plan claims raw-git disposable-sandbox writes have exactly 'two known sites' (eval_solver.py, criterion_preview.py), but at least two more Python sites issue a FLAGGED mutation verb (checkout) against disposable clone workspaces and are not enumerated: src/rebar/review_bot/gerrit_client.py:374 (`git checkout FETCH_HEAD`) and src/rebar/opcert_service/workspace.py:108 (`git checkout -q -B ...`) plus :125 (`git worktree add`). findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Add src/rebar/_store/push.py (its `_git` wrapper body + the merge/stash/checkout/rm --cached/fetch call sites) and src/rebar/_store/sync.py (its `_git` wrapper body + the reset --hard/merge/merge --abort call sites) to the enumerated seam-internal marking inventory, and correct the 'four wrapper names at HEAD' count to include push.py._git and sync.py._git.
evidence: Plan Scope: 'inline `# raw-git-ok: <reason>` markers on the enumerated seam internals (gitutil, lock, event_append, txn, purge_bridge, migration/bootstrap, reconciler git_adapter + _ref_lock)' — push.py and sync.py are absent.

src/rebar/_store/push.py:60 `def _git(base, *args, ...): return run_git(base, *args, check=False, env=env, timeout=_GIT_TIMEOUT)` then calls it with mutation verbs: line 100 `_git(base, 'rm', '-q', '--cached', ...)`, 101 `_git(base, 'checkout', 'HEAD', ...)`, 105 `_git(base, 'stash', 'drop', ...)`, 195 fetch, 214/240 `merge`, 227 `stash push`, 252/267 `merge --abort`, 253/262 `stash pop` — all against base_path (.../.tickets-tracker) under _lock.write_lock (line 199).

src/rebar/_store/sync.py:61 `def _git(tracker, *args): return run_git(tracker, *args, check=False, ...)` then line 155 `_git(tracker, 'reset', '--hard', remote, '--quiet')`, 172 `_git(tracker, 'merge', *extra, remote, ...)`, 182 `_git(tracker, 'merge', '--abort')` — under _lock.write_lock (line 245).

Under Approach R2: calls passing a mutation-verb string literal to the `_git` wrapper name fire via R2(a), and the `_git` body's `run_git(..., *args, ...)` opaque forwarding fires fail-closed via R2(c).
findings.finding: The plan's enumeration of store-seam-internal modules to mark ('gitutil, lock, event_append, txn, purge_bridge, migration/bootstrap, reconciler git_adapter + _ref_lock') omits two verified tracker-writing seam internals — src/rebar/_store/push.py and src/rebar/_store/sync.py — each of which fires under the plan's OWN Layer-P R2 rules but is not listed among the internals to receive a `# raw-git-ok:` marker.
findings.location: Scope bullet 2 ('inline # raw-git-ok markers on the enumerated seam internals (gitutil, lock, event_append, txn, purge_bridge, migration/bootstrap, reconciler git_adapter + _ref_lock)'); Approach '_git — the four wrapper names at HEAD'
scenarios: First full scan flags src/rebar/_store/push.py `_git` body (opaque *args → run_git) and its merge/stash/checkout/rm/reset call sites as unmarked bypasses; because push.py is not in the plan's marking inventory, either the tree is not clean at landing (AC #3 fails) or these seam-internal writes get erroneously remediated/removed.

First full scan flags src/rebar/_store/sync.py `_git` (opaque *args forwarding) plus its `reset --hard`/`merge`/`merge --abort` call sites; same outcome — an omitted seam internal whose absence from the inventory means the 'tree is clean at landing' AC cannot be satisfied as written.

AC #3 ('All enumerated seam internals (both seams) are marked with reasons; tree is clean at landing') is unmet as scoped, because push.py and sync.py are legitimate locked-store writers not enumerated for marking.

findings.finding: The Scope's committed inventory of seam internals to mark ("gitutil, lock, event_append, txn, purge_bridge, migration/bootstrap, reconciler git_adapter + _ref_lock") is incomplete: a codebase sweep for git mutation verbs finds several locked-store-write command internals with their own `_git()` wrappers that are neither enumerated nor covered by the named buckets — delete.py, compact.py, and fsck_repair.py. Each mutates the tracker under the write lock, so each will be flagged by Layer P and must carry a `# raw-git-ok: locked store seam internal` marker, but none is named as a marking target. The plan's Rationale further asserts "every raw mutation is a seam internal, a sandbox fixture, or a bypass", yet opcert_service/workspace.py and review_bot/gerrit_client.py issue raw mutations (worktree/remote add, checkout) that fit none of the three categories.
findings.location: Scope: "inline `# raw-git-ok: <reason>` markers on the enumerated seam internals (gitutil, lock, event_append, txn, purge_bridge, migration/bootstrap, reconciler git_adapter + _ref_lock)"
findings.suggested_fix: In Scope, expand the enumerated seam-internals list to include _commands/delete.py, _commands/compact.py, and _commands/fsck_repair.py (each mutates the tracker under the write lock via its own `_git`). In the Rationale, add a fourth category for ephemeral workspace provisioning (opcert_service/workspace.py, review_bot/gerrit_client.py `remote add`/`worktree add`/`checkout`) with its own marker reason, or explicitly classify those as disposable-clone sandbox writes.

findings.finding: R2's 'string literal anywhere in the call's arguments' will fire on non-index git subcommands where the literal 'add' is a subcommand argument (git worktree add, git remote add), a false-positive class the plan's verb list does not acknowledge.
scenarios: worktree/remote add sites fire and require markers or a subcommand-position rule; without acknowledgement the author may be surprised or add misleading 'locked store seam' reasons to sandbox/remote-config ops

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] State the lint's behavior on unparseable Python/YAML/shell files (fail-closed: emit an error rather than skip) so a parse failure cannot silently drop a file from coverage.
evidence: Layer P is 'Python, AST' and Layer W 'parse .github/workflows/*.yml run-blocks and scripts/*.sh' — neither states behavior on a parse error
The lint elsewhere adopts a fail-closed stance ('fail-closed, an OPAQUE argv ... fires') but does not extend that stance to unparseable files
findings.finding: The plan does not state how each lint layer behaves when a target file cannot be parsed (a Python module with a syntax error, or a malformed workflow YAML): fail-open (skip, silently missing any bypass in that file) or fail-closed (error). Given the lint's stated fail-closed posture on unresolvable argv, an unparseable file is the analogous edge case and its handling is unspecified.
findings.location: Approach (Layer P / Layer W) and Scope (scripts/check_raw_git_writes.py)
scenarios: A future PR adds a Python file with a transient syntax error containing a raw git commit against the tracker; if the AST parse throws and the lint fails-open, the bypass ships unflagged
A hand-edited workflow YAML with invalid indentation silently skips Layer W
findings.suggested_fix: Add to the Approach/lint-header: a file that fails to parse is reported as a lint error (fail-closed), not skipped, mirroring the opaque-argv fail-closed rule.

event_write_guard.py:20-22 — 'The live guard now ships as tests/unit/test_canonical.py' — an established seam-guard placement (unit test vs standalone scripts/ + inline marker) the plan does not weigh.
findings.finding: The plan crosses the novel-pattern bright-line (new two-layer AST+shell/YAML store-write-seam CI lint) but omits the closest existing prior art: docs/experiments/event_write_guard.py, a validated stdlib-only structural guard for the identical 'fail CI if a write bypasses the canonical seam' problem class, using the same Python-AST + bash two-prong design, the same local-variable dataflow tracking, and an allowlist sanction mechanism (its live descendant is tests/unit/test_canonical.py).
scenarios: Reviewer/author evaluating whether a standalone scripts/check_raw_git_writes.py + inline-marker design repackages an existing repo pattern rather than extending it.
Deciding allowlist-in-code (event_write_guard idiom) vs inline # raw-git-ok markers, and standalone-script vs live-guard-as-unit-test placement.

findings.finding: The plan enumerates src/rebar/_store/lock.py as a store-seam internal whose 'INTERNALS legitimately issue raw git' and lists it among the files to receive a `# raw-git-ok: <reason>` marker, but lock.py issues no git at all.
findings.location: Context/Problem + Scope: '_store/lock.py' listed under 'the store seam ... whose INTERNALS legitimately issue raw git'; Scope bullet 'inline markers on the enumerated seam internals (gitutil, lock, ...)'
findings.suggested_fix: Drop _store/lock.py from the raw-git seam-internal list; the lock-held raw git actually lives in _store/event_append.py (_run_git) and _commands/purge_bridge.py, which are already enumerated.

findings.finding: The plan lists src/rebar/_store/lock.py among the seam INTERNALS that 'legitimately issue raw git' and therefore need a `# raw-git-ok:` marker, but lock.py is implemented with fcntl+mkdir and issues no git mutation verb, so Layer P would find nothing there to mark — the marker target does not exist in that file.
findings.location: Context/Problem and Scope — enumerated seam internals include '_store/lock.py'

findings.finding: Layer P's stated detection rule ('flag any subprocess invocation whose argv contains git with a mutation verb') cannot flag most of the enumerated seam internals it directs authors to mark, because they route git through wrapper functions (run_git / run_git_write / _run_git / _git), not literal subprocess.run(['git', <verb>, ...]) calls. The premise that 'every raw mutation ... ALL of them get flagged by default' is refuted for those files.
findings.location: Approach, Layer P: 'flag any subprocess invocation whose argv contains git with a mutation verb ... UNLESS the line or enclosing function carries the marker'; and 'every raw mutation is a seam internal, a sandbox fixture, or a bypass. ALL of them get flagged by default'
findings.suggested_fix: Extend Layer P to treat calls to the known git-execution wrappers (run_git, run_git_write, _run_git, _git) whose first/argv element carries a mutation verb as raw-git mutations too, in addition to direct subprocess.run(['git',...]); then re-derive which enumerated files actually get flagged vs marked.

findings.finding: Layer P's detection rule ('flag any subprocess invocation whose argv contains git with a mutation verb') does not match the actual call shape of the seam internals the plan says to mark, nor of most codebase git writes: git_adapter.py, _ref_lock.py, event_append.py and txn.py issue git through the shared wrappers run_git/run_git_write/_run_git/_git, where the mutation verb is threaded as a positional/list-fragment arg and the literal 'git' token lives inside the wrapper — not in a subprocess.run(['git', ...]) argv at the call site.
findings.suggested_fix: Extend the Layer P detector to recognize the codebase's git wrapper call-shape — flag a call to subprocess.run/Popen OR to run_git/run_git_write/_run_git/_git whose first git-arg (after cwd) is a mutation verb, resolving list-literal fragments (e.g. args = ["update-ref", ...]) — and place the required seam-internal markers on those wrapper call sites accordingly.
